title: Crankshaft Position Sensor No Signal
problem: The ECU detects no normal signal from the crankshaft position sensor, which is essential for engine timing and RPM calculation.
symptoms: Engine will not start; Engine stalls immediately after starting; No spark
actions: Check CPS wiring for damage; Verify sensor resistance; Replace CPS if faulty
location: Near the crankshaft
column9: typically on the engine's left or right side cover

title: Intake Air Pressure Sensor (MAP) Open/Short
problem: The ECU detects an open or short circuit in the Intake Air Pressure Sensor, leading to incorrect air-fuel mixture calculations.
symptoms: Rough idle; Poor acceleration; Decreased fuel economy
actions: Inspect MAP sensor wiring and connector; Test sensor output voltage; Replace MAP sensor
location: Connected to the air intake manifold

title: Intake Air Pressure Sensor Hose Problem
problem: The ECU detects an abnormal pressure reading or a problem with the hose connecting the MAP sensor to the intake manifold.
symptoms: Engine runs poorly; Fluctuating idle; Decreased engine performance
actions: Check MAP sensor hose for cracks or disconnections; Clear any blockages in the hose; Ensure proper vacuum seal
location: Hose connects the MAP sensor to the intake manifold

title: Throttle Position Sensor (TPS) Open/Short
problem: The ECU detects an open or short circuit in the Throttle Position Sensor, providing incorrect throttle angle information.
symptoms: Hesitation on acceleration; Unstable idle; Engine may rev unexpectedly
actions: Inspect TPS wiring and connector; Check TPS output voltage range; Replace TPS if out of specification
location: Mounted directly on the throttle body

title: Throttle Position Sensor Stuck
problem: The ECU detects that the throttle position sensor signal is not changing despite throttle input, indicating it's stuck.
symptoms: Poor throttle response; Engine speed remains constant; Cruise control issues (if equipped)
actions: Check TPS for mechanical sticking; Verify sensor movement; Replace TPS
location: Mounted directly on the throttle body

title: Sidestand Switch Malfunction
problem: The sidestand switch circuit has an open or short, preventing the engine from starting or cutting power when in gear.
symptoms: Engine won't start; Engine cuts out when selecting gear; Immobilizer light may illuminate
actions: Inspect sidestand switch wiring; Test switch continuity; Adjust or replace sidestand switch
location: Attached to the sidestand pivot point

title: Atmospheric Pressure Sensor Open/Short
problem: The ECU detects an open or short circuit in the atmospheric pressure sensor, affecting altitude compensation for fuel.
symptoms: Reduced performance at varying altitudes; Poor fuel economy; Engine running rich or lean
actions: Inspect APS wiring and connector; Test sensor output; Replace APS
location: Often integrated into the ECU or a separate sensor near the airbox

title: Coolant Temperature Sensor Open/Short
problem: The ECU detects an open or short circuit in the engine coolant temperature sensor, leading to incorrect fuel mixture.
symptoms: Hard starting when cold; Rich or lean running condition; Cooling fan not operating correctly
actions: Check CTS wiring and connector; Test sensor resistance; Replace CTS
location: Threaded into the cylinder head or thermostat housing

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Open/Short
problem: The ECU detects an open or short circuit in the intake air temperature sensor, affecting fuel mixture calculations.
symptoms: Poor fuel economy; Engine running rich or lean; Reduced engine performance
actions: Inspect IATS wiring and connector; Test sensor resistance; Replace IATS
location: Located in the air box or intake tract

title: O2 Sensor Heater Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects a fault in the heater circuit of the oxygen sensor, preventing it from reaching operating temperature quickly.
symptoms: Increased emissions; Decreased fuel efficiency; Check Engine Light (MIL) on
actions: Check O2 sensor heater wiring; Test heater resistance; Replace O2 sensor
location: Mounted in the exhaust pipe before the catalytic converter

title: O2 Sensor Input Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an abnormal signal from the oxygen sensor, indicating incorrect exhaust gas composition readings.
symptoms: Fluctuating idle; Poor fuel economy; Engine running rich or lean
actions: Inspect O2 sensor wiring; Check for exhaust leaks; Replace O2 sensor if faulty
location: Mounted in the exhaust pipe before the catalytic converter

title: Lean Angle Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an abnormal signal from the lean angle sensor, designed to cut the engine in case of a tip-over.
symptoms: Engine won't start; Engine cuts out randomly; Intermittent power loss
actions: Check sensor mounting and position; Inspect wiring for damage; Replace lean angle sensor
location: Often under the seat or fairing
column9: typically near the center of gravity

title: Speed Sensor No Signal
problem: The ECU is not receiving a signal from the speed sensor, which can affect speedometer readings and other speed-dependent systems.
symptoms: Speedometer not working; Odometer not counting; Reduced ABS/Traction Control function
actions: Inspect sensor wiring; Check sensor for debris; Replace speed sensor if faulty
location: Typically on the front or rear wheel
column9: near the brake rotor or sprocket

title: Speed Sensor or Neutral Switch Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an issue with the vehicle speed sensor or the neutral switch, affecting speed input and gear detection.
symptoms: Speedometer erratic; Difficult to shift; Engine cuts out at low speed
actions: Check sensor wiring; Test neutral switch continuity; Replace faulty component
location: Speed sensor on wheel
column9: neutral switch near gearbox output shaft

title: Fuel System Voltage Malfunction
affectedPart: Fuel Pump Relay / Fuel Pump / Wiring
problem: The ECU detects abnormal voltage in the fuel pump system, potentially affecting fuel pressure and delivery.
symptoms: Hard starting; Engine stalls; Reduced engine power; Check Engine Light (MIL) on
actions: Check battery voltage; Inspect fuel pump relay; Verify wiring to fuel pump
location: Fuel pump inside the fuel tank; relay usually near battery or fuse box

title: ECU EEPROM Error or Battery Voltage Monitor Error
problem: The ECU has detected an internal EEPROM (memory) error or an abnormal battery voltage reading to its power supply.
symptoms: Intermittent starting issues; Random warning lights; Engine performance issues
actions: Check battery voltage and charging system; Inspect ECU connectors; ECU replacement may be necessary
location: ECU under the seat or fairing

title: Air Cut-Off Valve Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an error with the air cut-off valve, which controls air flow for emissions or engine braking.
symptoms: Popping on deceleration; Emissions issues; Minor idle fluctuations
actions: Check ACV wiring and hose; Test ACV solenoid; Replace ACV if faulty
location: On the airbox or intake manifold

title: Power Supply to ECU Not Normal
problem: The voltage supplied to the ECU is outside the normal operating range, indicating a power supply issue.
symptoms: Engine won't start; ECU loses power; Intermittent electrical issues
actions: Check battery condition and terminals; Inspect main relay; Trace power supply wiring
location: Battery
column9: main relay (often near the battery or fuse box)

title: ECU Internal Malfunction
problem: The ECU has detected an internal fault within its own circuitry, preventing proper engine management.
symptoms: Engine won't start; Multiple system failures; Bike completely dead
actions: Check all ECU connectors; Verify ECU power and ground; ECU replacement is typically required
location: Under the seat or fairing

title: Main Relay Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects a fault with the main relay, which controls power to various engine management components.
symptoms: Engine won't start; No power to fuel pump; No ignition spark
actions: Check main relay wiring; Test relay continuity; Replace main relay
location: Often near the battery or fuse box

title: ABS Control Unit Communication Error
problem: The main ECU is unable to communicate with the Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) control unit.
symptoms: ABS warning light illuminated; ABS system inoperative; Brake performance may feel normal
actions: Check ABS unit wiring and connectors; Inspect wheel speed sensors; Consult dealer for ABS diagnostics
location: ABS control unit often near the front wheel or under the tank/seat

title: ABS Unit Internal Error
problem: The ABS control unit has detected an internal malfunction, rendering the ABS system inoperative.
symptoms: ABS warning light illuminated; Brakes lock up under hard braking; No ABS function
actions: Verify power and ground to ABS unit; Check for sensor ring damage; ABS unit replacement usually required
location: ABS control unit
column9: typically near the front wheel or under the tank/seat

title: Ride Control System Communication Error
affectedPart: Ride Control ECU / Main ECU / Wiring
problem: The main ECU has lost communication with a dedicated ride control system ECU (e.g., electronic suspension, traction control).
symptoms: Ride modes unavailable; Suspension not adjusting; Traction control inoperative
actions: Check wiring between ECUs; Inspect connectors; Consult dealer for system diagnosis
location: Varies
column9: typically between the main ECU and a separate control module

title: Auxiliary Sensor Communication Error
problem: warning
symptoms: The ECU is unable to communicate with an auxiliary sensor, such as an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) on advanced models.
actions: Traction control not working; Cornering ABS inoperative; Advanced rider aids disabled
location: Check sensor wiring and connection; Inspect sensor for physical damage; Consult dealer for specific sensor diagnostics
column10: under the seat or near the swingarm pivot

title: ECU Communication Error (Meter to ECU)
problem: The meter unit cannot establish communication with the ECU, indicating a serious communication fault.
symptoms: Dash displays ""Er-1""; No gauge readings; Engine may not start
actions: Check wiring harness between meter and ECU; Inspect connectors for corrosion; Test ECU and meter unit communication lines
location: Wiring harness connecting the instrument cluster (meter) to the ECU

title: ECU Communication Error (ECU to Meter)
problem: The ECU is unable to communicate with the meter unit, preventing data display on the dashboard.
symptoms: Dash displays ""Er-2""; No gauge readings; Warning lights may not function
actions: Check wiring harness between meter and ECU; Inspect connectors; Test ECU and meter unit communication lines
location: Wiring harness connecting the ECU to the instrument cluster (meter)

title: Communication Error Between Meter and Immobilizer Unit
problem: The meter unit and immobilizer unit are failing to communicate, which prevents the engine from starting.
symptoms: Engine won't start; Immobilizer light flashes; Key not recognized
actions: Check wiring between meter and immobilizer; Verify immobilizer unit power; Re-program keys if necessary
location: Wiring harness connecting the instrument cluster and immobilizer antenna ring

title: YCC-T Throttle Grip Position Sensor Error
problem: The Yamaha Chip Controlled Throttle (YCC-T) system detects an error with the throttle grip position sensor.
symptoms: No throttle response; Engine enters limp mode; Engine light illuminated
actions: Inspect throttle grip sensor wiring; Test sensor output; Replace throttle grip assembly
location: Handlebar

title: YCC-T Throttle Valve Position Sensor Error
problem: The YCC-T system detects an error with the throttle valve position sensor at the throttle body.
symptoms: Incorrect throttle response; Engine enters limp mode; Unstable idle
actions: Inspect throttle valve sensor wiring; Check for mechanical sticking; Replace throttle body or sensor
location: On the throttle body

title: YCC-T ECU Monitor Error
problem: The ECU's internal monitoring system for the YCC-T (ride-by-wire) system has detected a malfunction.
symptoms: No throttle response; Engine power severely limited; System shutdown
actions: Check all YCC-T related sensors and actuators; Inspect ECU for internal faults; ECU replacement may be required
location: Internal to the ECU

title: YCC-T Throttle Valve Stuck
problem: The YCC-T system detects that the throttle valve is mechanically stuck or unable to move freely.
symptoms: Uncommanded acceleration; Engine won't idle; No throttle response
actions: Inspect throttle body for obstructions; Clean throttle valve; Replace throttle body if damaged
location: Inside the throttle body

title: Immobilizer System Malfunction
problem: The immobilizer system has detected a fault, preventing the engine from starting due to key recognition issues.
symptoms: Engine won't start; Immobilizer light flashes rapidly; Key not recognized
actions: Try a different registered key; Check immobilizer antenna wiring; Consult dealer for system diagnosis
location: Immobilizer unit often integrated with the ECU or a separate module; antenna ring around the ignition barrel
